I couldn't reproduce the bug, so I didn't change anything. In `src/slugify.py`, `slugify('Hello,  World!')` already returns `'hello-world'`. All 5 tests in the repo pass.

The current code (`re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text).strip("-")`) collapses runs of punctuation and spaces into one dash and trims dashes from both ends. The reported output, `'hello---world-'`, looks like what you'd get from replacing each non-alphanumeric character individually (`[^a-z0-9]` with no `+`) and not stripping the ends. That suggests the users may be running an older version or a different copy of the function.

Things worth checking:
- **Version:** whether the reporters are on a release or deployment older than this code.
- **Other copies:** whether another `slugify` exists elsewhere, such as a vendored copy or a separate package. A search of this repo found only `src/slugify.py`.

If you can tell me where the report came from, I can look further. I can also add a regression test for `'Hello,  World!'` so this case stays covered.
